    #Part 1 - Set 1 (Longitudinal Static Stability)

    #Question 4

    Wing pitching moment equation,

    Cmw​​=Cmacw​​​+CLw​​(cˉxCG​−xac​​)

    Cmw​​=−0.015+0.5(cˉ0.05cˉ​)

    Cmw​​=0.01

    #Question 5

    #Part (a)

    Wing pitching moment equation,

    Cmw​​=Cmacw​​​+CLw​​(cˉxCG​−xac​​)

    Wing pitching moment coefficient,

    Cmw​​=21​ρV2ScˉMw​​

    Cmw​​=21​(1.23)(100)2(1.5)(0.45)−12.4​

    Cmw​​=−0.0029871

    Pitching moment about the ac,

    −0.0029871=Cmacw​​​+0

    Cmacw​​​=−0.0029871

    #Part (b)

    Wing pitching moment coefficient,

    Cmw​​=21​ρV2ScˉMCGw​​​

    Cmw​​=21​(1.23)(100)2(1.5)(0.45)20.67​

    Cmw​​=0.0049792

    Wing lift coefficient,

    CLw​​=21​ρV2SL​

    CLw​​=21​(1.23)(100)2(1.5)3675​

    CLw​​=0.39837

    Distance between CG and ac,

    0.0049792=−0.0029871+0.39837(cˉxCG​−xac​​)

    cˉxCG​−xac​​=0.019997

    xCG​−xac​=0.02cˉ

    Since the RHS is positive, then xCG​>xac​.
    The CG is located 2% mean chord aft of the ac.

    Note that the pitching moment about the ac is constant.
    The     ac is the point about which pitching moment is constant.

    For the wing to be stable,

    Cmαw​​​<0

    CLαw​​​(cˉxCG​−xac​​)<0

    xCG​−xac​<0

    xCG​<xac​

    The wing is only stable if the CG is located forward of the ac.
    Thus, since xCG​>xac​, the wing is not stable.

    #Question 6

    Given information (wing):

    • iw​=1°
    • αabsw​​=5°
    • α0w​​=−1°
    • Lw​=4134 N (Lift at αabsw​​=5°)
    • Sw​=1.5 m2 (From Question 5)
    • cˉ=0.45 m (From Question 5)

    Given information (tail):

    • lt​=1 m
    • St​=0.4 m2
    • it​=−1°
    • CLαt​​​=0.15/deg
    • ηH​=0.8

    Pitching moment equations,

    Cm​=Cmf​​+Cmw​​+Cmt​​

    Cmw​​=Cm0w​​​+Cmαw​​​αw​

    Cmt​​=Cm0t​​​+Cmαt​​​αw​

    Relations between angles of attack,

    αFRL​=αw​−iw​

    αabsw​​=αw​−α0w​​

    αt​=αFRL​−ε+it​

    Fuselage contribution

    Fuselage angle of attack,

    αFRL​=αw​−iw​

    αFRL​=4°−1°

    αFRL​=3°

    Fuselage pitching moment,

    Cmf​​=−0.02+0.01αFRL​

    Cmf​​=−0.02+0.01(3°)

    Cmf​​=0.01

    Wing contribution

    Wing pitching moment components,

    Cm0w​​​=Cmacw​​​+CL0w​​​(cˉxCG​−xac​​)

    Cmαw​​​=CLαw​​​(cˉxCG​−xac​​)

    From Question 5,

    Cmacw​​​=−0.0029871

    Wing angle of attack,

    αw​=αabsw​​+α0w​​

    αw​=5°+(−1°)

    αw​=4°

    Wing lift coefficient,

    CLw​​=21​ρV2SL​

    CLw​​=21​(1.23)(100)2(1.5)4134​

    CLw​​=0.44813

    Wing lift curve slope,

    CLαw​​​=dαw​dCLw​​​=αw​−α0w​​CLw​​−0​

    CLαw​​​=4°−(−1°)0.44814−0​

    CLαw​​​=0.089626/deg

    Wing lift curve intercept,

    CLw​​=CL0w​​​+CLαw​​​αw​

    0.44813=CL0w​​​+0.089626(4°)

    CL0w​​​=0.089626

    Distance between CG and ac,

    xCG​−xac​=0.02cˉ+0.04

    xCG​−xac​=0.02(0.45)+0.04

    xCG​−xac​=0.049 m

    Wing pitching moment components,

    Cm0w​​​=−0.0029871+0.089626(0.450.049​)=0.0067722

    Cmαw​​​=0.089626(0.450.049​)=0.0097593

    Wing pitching moment,

    Cmw​​=0.0067722+0.0097593(4°)=0.045809

    Tail contribution

    Tail pitching moment components,

    Cm0t​​​=ηH​VH​CLαt​​​(ε0​+iw​−it​)

    Cmαt​​​=−ηH​VH​CLαt​​​(1−dαdε​)

    Horizontal tail volume ratio,

    VH​=clt​​⋅Sw​St​​

    VH​=0.451​⋅1.50.4​

    VH​=0.59259

    Tail pitching moment components,

    Cm0t​​​=0.8(0.59259)(0.15)[0+1°−(−1°)]=0.14222

    Cmαt​​​=−0.8(0.59259)(0.15)(1−0.35)=−0.046222

    Tail pitching moment,

    Cmt​​=0.14222−0.046222(4°)=−0.042668

    Total pitching moment,

    Cm​=Cmf​​+Cmw​​+Cmt​​

    Cm​=0.01+0.045809−0.042668=0.013141

    Pitching moment about the CG,

    MCG​=21​ρV2ScˉCm​

    MCG​=21​(1.23)(100)2(1.5)(0.45)(0.013141)

    MCG​=54.552 Nm

    #Question 7

    #Part (a) + Part (b) + Part (c)

    From Question 6,

    Cmf​​=−0.03+0.01αw​

    Cmw​​=0.0067722+0.0097593αw​

    Cmt​​=0.14222−0.046222αw​

    Note that equations are in terms of αw​.

    Fuselage pitching moment,

    Cmf​​=−0.02+0.01αFRL​

    Cmf​​=−0.02+0.01(αw​−iw​)

    Cmf​​=−0.02+0.01(αw​−1°)

    Cmf​​=−0.03+0.01αw​

    Total pitching moment,

    Cm​=Cmf​​+Cmw​​+Cmt​​

    Cm​=0.11899−0.026463αw​

    From the above equation,

    Cm0​​=0.11899

    Cm(αw​)​​=−0.026463

    For longitudinal static stability, Cm(αw​)​​<0. (Negative slope)
    To trim at positive angles of attack, Cm0​​>0. (Positive intercept)
    Since both conditions are satisfied, the model is stable and trimmable.

    Trim angle of attack, where Cm​=0,

    0=0.11899−0.026463αw​

    0=0.11899−0.026463(αFRL​+iw​)

    0=0.11899−0.026463(αFRL​+1°)

    αFRL​=3.4965°

    #Part (d)

    Lift Generated by Wing

    Wing angle of attack,

    αw​=αFRL​+iw​

    αw​=3.4965°+1°

    αw​=4.4965°

    Wing lift coefficient,

    CLw​​=CL0w​​​+CLαw​​​αw​

    CLw​​=0.089626+0.089626(4.4965°)

    CLw​​=0.49263

    Lift generated by the wing,

    Lw​=21​ρVw​2Sw​CLw​​

    Lw​=21​(1.23)(100)2(1.5)(0.49263)

    Lw​=4544.5 N

    Lift Generated by Tail

    Tail angle of attack,

    αt​=αFRL​−ε+it​

    αt​=αw​−iw​−(ε0​+dαdε​αw​)+it​

    αt​=4.4965°−1°−[0+0.35(4.4965°)]+(−1°)

    αt​=0.92273°

    Tail lift coefficient,

    CLt​​=CLαt​​​αt​

    CLt​​=0.15(0.92273°)

    CLt​​=0.13841

    Lift generated by the tail,

    Lt​=21​ρVt​2St​CLt​​

    Lt​=(ηH​21​ρVw​2)St​CLt​​

    Lt​=21​(0.8)(1.23)(100)2(0.4)(0.13841)

    Lt​=272.39 N

    #Part 2 - Set 2 (Linear Systems Theory)

    #Question 1

    #Part (a)

    At the equilibrium point, X¨=0 and X˙=0.

    0=X¨−(1−X2)X˙+X

    0=0−(1−Xe​2)0+Xe​

    Xe​=0

    Taking small variations about the equilibrium point,

    X=Xe​+ΔX=ΔX

    X˙=X˙e​+ΔX˙=ΔX˙

    X¨=X¨e​+ΔX¨=ΔX¨

    Substituting into the original equation,

    0=ΔX¨−(1−ΔX2)ΔX˙+ΔX

    0=ΔX¨−ΔX˙+ΔX

    Note that higher-order terms are ignored as
    the product of small values is even smaller.

    Shifting the origin to the equilibrium point,

    0=X¨−X˙+X

    #Part (b)

    Linearized equation is a 2nd-order ODE.

    0=X¨−X˙+X

    Characteristic equation of ODE,

    0=aλ2+bλ+c

    0=λ2−λ+1

    whereby a, b, c are the coefficients of the ODE

    Roots of the characteristic equation,

    λ1,2​=2a−b±b2−4ac​​

    λ1,2​=2(1)−(−1)±(−1)2−4(1)(1)​​

    λ1,2​=21​±j23​​

    Since the roots are complex, solution is in the form,

    X=eαt(Asinβt+Bcosβt)

    X=e21​t(Asin23​​t+Bsin23​​t)

    whereby α≡ real part and β≡ imaginary part

    As t→∞, the exponential term tends towards infinity (unstable).
    As t→∞, the sinusoidal terms is oscillatory (neutrally stable).
    Thus, the overall solution is unstable.

    #Question 2

    #Part (a)

    Let x1​=X and x2​=X˙.

    Differentiating w.r.t. time,

    x˙1​=X˙=x2​

    x˙2​=X¨

    Substituting into the original equation,

    0=X¨−(1−X2)X˙+X

    0=x˙2​−(1−x1​2)x2​+x1​

    0=x˙2​−x2​+x1​2x2​+x1​

    x˙2​=−x1​+(1−x1​2)x2​

    The two 1st-order ODE are,

    f1​(x1​,x2​)≡x˙1​=x2​

    f2​(x1​,x2​)≡x˙2​=−x1​+(1−x1​2)x2​

    #Part (b)

    Jacobian matrix,

    A=∂X∂F​​X0​​

    A=[0−1−2x1​x2​​11−x1​2​]x1​=0, x2​=0​

    A=[0−1​11​]

    Linearized equation in state-space form,

    ΔX˙=AΔX

    {Δx˙1​Δx˙2​​}=[0−1​11​]{Δx1​Δx2​​}

    #Part (c)

    Characteristic equation of linearized equation,

    det​A−λI​​=0

    det​−λ−1​11−λ​​=0

    −λ(1−λ)−(−1)(1)=0

    λ2−λ+1=0

    Roots of the characteristic equation,

    λ1,2​=2a−b±b2−4ac​​

    λ1,2​=2(1)−(−1)±(−1)2−4(1)(1)​​

    λ1,2​=21​±j23​​

    Since the roots are complex, solution is in the form,

    X=eαt(Asinβt+Bcosβt)

    X=e21​t(Asin23​​t+Bsin23​​t)

    whereby α≡ real part and β≡ imaginary part

    As t→∞, the exponential term tends towards infinity (unstable).
    As t→∞, the sinusoidal terms is oscillatory (neutrally stable).
    Thus, the overall solution is unstable.

    #Question 3

    #Part (a)

    Let x1​=θ and x2​=θ˙.

    Differentiating w.r.t. time,

    x˙1​=θ˙=x2​

    x˙2​=θ¨

    Substituting into the original equation,

    0=x˙2​+mkd​​x2​+lg​sin(x1​)

    x˙2​=−mkd​​x2​−lg​sin(x1​)

    The two 1st-order ODE are,

    f1​(x1​,x2​)≡x˙1​=x2​

    f2​(x1​,x2​)≡x˙2​=−mkd​​x2​−lg​sin(x1​)

    #Part (b)

    Jacobian matrix,

    A=∂X∂F​​X0​​

    A=[0−lg​cos(x1​)​1−mkd​​​]x1​=0, x2​=0​

    A=[0−lg​​1−mkd​​​]

    Linearized equation in state-space form,

    ΔX˙=AΔX

    {x˙1​x˙2​​}=[0−lg​​1−mkd​​​]{x1​x2​​}

    #Part (c)

    Characteristic equation of linearized equation,

    det​A−λI​​=0

    det​−λ−lg​​1−mkd​​−λ​​=0

    −λ(−mkd​​−λ)−(−lg​)(1)=0

    λ2+mkd​​λ+lg​=0

    Roots of the characteristic equation,

    λ1,2​=2a−b±b2−4ac​​

    λ1,2​=−2mkd​​±4m2kd​2​−lg​​

    For an overdamped system,

    4m2kd​2​−lg​>0

    2mkd​​>lg​​

    kd​>2mlg​​

    For an underdamped system,

    4m2kd​2​−lg​<0

    2mkd​​<lg​​

    kd​<2mlg​​

    For a critically damped system,

    4m2kd​2​−lg​=0

    2mkd​​=lg​​

    kd​=2mlg​​

    For system to be stable, the real parts of
    the roots must be negative such that the roots lie on the left plane of the pole plot.

    #Question 4

    Let x1​=y, x2​=y′ and x3​=y′′.

    Differentiating w.r.t. time,

    x˙1​=y′=x2​

    x˙2​=y′′=x3​

    x˙3​=y′′′

    Substituting into the original equation,

    u=x˙3​+3x3​+2x2​

    x˙3​=−3x3​−2x2​+u

    The three 1st-order ODE are,

    f1​(x1​,x2​,x3​)≡x˙1​=x2​

    f2​(x1​,x2​,x3​)≡x˙2​=x3​

    f3​(x1​,x2​,x3​)≡x˙3​=−3x3​−2x2​+u

    Expressing in state-space form x˙=Ax+Bu,

    ⎩⎨⎧​x˙1​x˙2​x˙3​​⎭⎬⎫​=​000​10−2​01−3​​⎩⎨⎧​x1​x2​x3​​⎭⎬⎫​+​001​​u

    #Question 5

    Let x1​=y1​ and x2​=y˙​1​.

    Differentiating w.r.t. time,

    x˙1​=y˙​1​=x2​

    x˙2​=y¨​1​

    Substituting into the equation,

    0=mx˙2​+cx2​+k(x1​−x3​)

    x˙2​=−mc​x2​−mk​(x1​−x3​)

    Let x3​=y2​ and x4​=y˙​2​.

    Differentiating w.r.t. time,

    x˙3​=y˙​2​=x4​

    x˙4​=y¨​2​

    Substituting into the equation,

    F=mx˙4​+k(x3​−x1​)

    x˙4​=mF​−mk​(x3​−x1​)

    The four 1st-order ODE are,

    f1​≡x˙1​=x2​

    f3​≡x˙3​=x4​

    f4​≡x˙4​=mF​−mk​(x3​−x1​)

    Expressing in state-space form,

    ⎩⎨⎧​x˙1​x˙2​x˙3​x˙4​​⎭⎬⎫​=​0−k/m0k/m​1−c/m00​0k/m0−k/m​0010​​⎩⎨⎧​x1​x2​x3​x4​​⎭⎬⎫​+​000k/m​​F

    #Question 6

    x˙1​=y˙​1​=x2​

    #Question 7

    Performing Laplace transform,

    ms2Y(s)+csY(s)=F(s)

    (ms2+cs)Y(s)=F(s)

    Y(s)=ms2+csF(s)​

    Impulse Input

    For an impulse input,

    Y(s)=ms2+cs1​

    Y(s)=s2+(c/m)s1/m​

    Y(s)=s(s+c/m)1/m​

    Y(s)=m1​(sA​+s+c/mB​)

    Solving the partial fractions,

    1=A(s+mc​)+Bs

    A=cm​

    B=−cm​

    Step Input

    For a step input,

    Y(s)=ms2+cs1/s​

    Y(s)=s1​⋅s2+(c/m)s1/m​

    Y(s)=m1​⋅s2(s+c/m)1​

    Y(s)=m1​(sA​+s+c/mB​+s2C​)

    Solving the partial fractions,

    1=As(s+mc​)+Bs2+C(s+mc​)

    A=−c2m2​

    B=c2m2​

    C=cm​

    Response of the system,

    Y(s)unit​=m1​(sm/c​−s+c/mm/c​)=c1​(s1​−s+c/m1​)

    Y(s)step​=m1​(−sm2/c2​+s+c/mm2/c2​+s2m/c​)

    Performing inverse Laplace transform,

    y(t)unit​=c1​[1−e−(c/m)t]

    y(t)step​=m1​[−c2m2​+c2m2​e−(c/m)t+cm​t]

    #Question 11

    Let x1​=x and x2​=x˙.

    Let x3​=θ and x4​=θ˙.

    Differentiating w.r.t. time,

    x˙1​=x˙=x2​

    x˙3​=θ˙=x4​

    x˙2​=x¨

    x˙4​=θ¨

    Assuming small angle approximation,

    0=lθ¨+x¨cosθ−gsinθ

    0=lθ¨+x¨(1)−g(θ)

    0=lθ¨+x¨−gθ

    gx3​=lx˙4​+x˙2​

    Ignoring higher-order terms and assuming small angle approximation,

    F(t)=(M+m)x¨+mlθ¨cosθ−mlθ˙2sinθ

    F(t)=(M+m)x¨+mlθ¨(1)−ml(0)(θ)

    F(t)=(M+m)x¨+mlθ¨

    F(t)=(M+m)x˙2​+mlx˙4​

    The above equations are not in state-space form, whereby the LHS
    has only one derivative term, and the RHS has no derivative terms.

    Expressing the equations of motion as a matrix,

    {gx3​F(t)​}=[1M+m​lml​]{x˙2​x˙4​​}

    Using Cramer’s rule,

    x˙2​=ml−l(M+m)(gx3​)(ml)−l⋅F(t)​

    x˙2​=−Mmgx3​−F(t)​

    x˙2​=−Mmg​x3​+MF(t)​

    #Question 12

    #Part (a)

    Let x1​=x and x2​=x˙.

    Differentiating w.r.t. time,

    x˙1​=x˙=x2​

    x˙2​=x¨

    Substituting into the original equation,

    x˙2​=−mc​x2​−mk​x1​+mF(t)​

    #Part (b)

    Characteristic equation,

    det​A−λI​​=0

    det​−λ−mk​​1−mc​−λ​​=0

    −λ(−mc​−λ)−(−mk​)=0

    λ2+mc​λ+mk​=0

    Rewriting the characteristic equation,

    λ2+(2ζωn​)λ+ωn​2=0

    where ωn​=mk​​ and ζ=ccr​c​=2mωn​c​

    Roots of the characteristic equation,

    λ1,2​=2a−b±b2−4ac​​

    λ1,2​=2−2ζωn​±4ζ2ωn​2−4ωn​2​​

    λ1,2​=−ζωn​±ωn​ζ2−1​

    For an overdamped system, where ζ>1,

    λ1,2​=−ζωn​±ωn​ζ2−1​

    Two real and distinct roots.

    For a critically damped system, where ζ=1,

    λ1,2​=−ζωn​

    Two real and repeating roots.

    For an underdamped system, where 0<ζ<1,

    λ1,2​=−ζωn​±jωn​1−ζ2​

    Two complex and distinct roots.

    For an undamped system, where ζ=0,

    λ1,2​=±jωn​

    Two imaginary and distinct roots.
